Determine whether this paper directly establishes our Mersenne-weight criterion, a stronger nonsquare/odd-valuation theorem for our norm N_e, or only primitive-divisor counts. Check exact hypotheses, signs, exceptional cases and e versus 2e indexing. Read the actual paper, not just your earlier secondary restatement in Juricevic. Correct any inaccuracies in that restatement comparison.

Your immediately preceding bounded-pass report is board message 24 in discussion 9. The dispatcher has not yet integrated that report into the committed ledger; do not assume the repository contains its details. Your report said the secondary restatement gives >=2 primitive divisors for odd n divisible by 3, n>=9, with kappa=-3 and eta=1. Verify this against the ORIGINAL theorem and distinguish the original's conditional/asymptotic bound from the thesis's explicit effective cutoff. Do not promote counts to odd valuations.

Notation: lambda=sqrt(3)+sqrt(2); for odd n, U_n=(lambda^n+lambda^-n)/(2sqrt(3))=1,9,89,881,8721,... . First Lehmer (L,M)=(8,-1) has roots lambda,-lambda^-1; associated (R,Q)=(12,1) has roots lambda,lambda^-1. First Lehmer (12,1) gives W_n. Ordinary Lucas recurrence x_(n+2)=10*x_(n+1)-x_n gives U_n*W_n at odd n and does not isolate U_n.

For odd e>1, N_e=Norm_Ke(C_e^2+8)=prod_(d|e) U_d^mu(e/d)=Phi_e(lambda,-lambda^-1)=Phi_(2e)(lambda,lambda^-1). This is a primitive homogeneous cyclotomic factor, not generally the whole term U_e. A primitive divisor count without odd valuation cannot establish nonsquareness.

Our exact criterion: ell=2^t-1 prime, odd t>=3; w(p)=2^(v2(p^2-1)-3) for distinct odd source primes p. If sum_(p|e)w(p)=2^(t-2), then Legendre(N_e/ell)=-1 for every positive exponent vector. A separate necessary norm-square argument excludes sqrt(C_e^2+8) from every cyclotomic field for those orders. If you find a stronger known theorem, give its exact statement and substitution, with e=3, powers of 3, and N_e versus its 3-stripped value treated explicitly.

Deliver a short plain-English conclusion, followed by page/theorem numbers, exact applicability analysis and ready-to-use corrections for the literature review/source ledger. Identify tools from the original that might help the general norm proof even if they do not subsume our theorem. Distinguish an actual theorem from a conjecture/problem or proof ingredient. Keep the 1986 Patras chapter marked full-text unread; do not search indefinitely or restart broad novelty research. A negative comparison is not proof of novelty.
